word_for_word: उक्ताः संक्षेपतः पूर्वं सप्तमादौ विभूतयः। दशमे ता वितन्यन्ते सर्वत्रेश्वरदृष्टये।।1।।एवं तावत्सप्तमादिभिस्त्रिभिरध्यायैर्भजनीयं परमेश्वररूपं निरूपितम्। तद्विभूतयश्च सप्तमेरसोऽहमप्सु कौन्तेय इत्यादिना संक्षेपतो दर्शिताः। अष्टमे चअधियज्ञोऽहमेवात्र इत्यादिना? नवमे चअहं ऋतुरहं यज्ञः इत्यादिना। अथेदानीं ता एव विभूतीः प्रपञ्चयिष्यन् स्वभक्तेश्चावश्यंकरणीयत्वं वर्णयिष्यन् श्रीभगवानुवाच -- भूय एवेति। महान्तौ युद्धादिस्वधर्मानुष्ठाने महत्परिचर्यायां वा कुशलौ बाहू यस्य हे महाबाहो? भूयएव पुनरपि मे वचः शृणु। कथंभूतम्। परमं परमात्मनिष्ठं मद्वचनामृतेनैव प्रीतिं प्राप्नुवते ते तुभ्यं हितकाम्यया हितेच्छया यदहं वक्ष्यामि तत्।

The divine manifestations were stated briefly earlier beginning in the seventh chapter; in the tenth they are expanded so that the Lord may be seen everywhere. In the three chapters beginning with the seventh, the form of the Supreme Lord fit to be worshipped was described, and His manifestations were indicated briefly by statements such as ‘I am the taste in water,’ in the eighth by ‘I alone am the adhiyajña here,’ and in the ninth by ‘I am the rite, I am the sacrifice.’ Now, intending to expand those manifestations and to describe the indispensable nature of devotion to Himself, the Blessed Lord says ‘Again indeed.’ O mighty-armed—one whose arms are skilled in performing one’s great duty such as battle, or in great service—again hear My supreme word, established in the Supreme Self, which I shall speak to you out of desire for your welfare, because you take delight in the nectar of My words alone.

उक्तस्यापि पुनर्वचने दुर्ज्ञेयत्वं हेतुमाह -- न म इति। मे मम प्रकृष्टं भवं जन्मरहितस्यापि नानाविभूतिभिराविर्भावं सुरगणा अपि महर्षयो भृग्वादयोऽपि न जानन्ति। तत्र हेतुःअहं हि देवानां महर्षीणां चादिः कारणम्? सर्वशः सर्वप्रकारैरुत्पादकत्वेन बुद्ध्यादिप्रवर्तकत्वेन च। अतो मदनुग्रहं विना मां केऽपि न जानन्तीत्यर्थः।

He gives the reason for repeating what was already said: it is difficult to know. Neither the hosts of gods nor great seers such as Bhṛgu know My supreme manifestation, My appearing through many manifestations though I am unborn. The reason is that I am the origin and cause of the gods and great seers in every respect, both as their producer and as the impeller of their intellect and other faculties. Therefore no one knows Me without My grace.
एवंभूतात्मज्ञाने फलमाह -- यो मामिति। सर्वकारणत्वादेव न विद्यते आदिः कारणं यस्य तमनादिम्। अतएवाजं जन्मशून्यं लोकानां महेश्वरं च मां यो वेत्ति स मनुष्येष्वसंमूढः संमोहरहतिः सन्सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते।

He states the fruit of knowing Him in this way. Because I am the cause of everything, I have no prior cause and am beginningless; therefore I am unborn, free from birth, and the great Lord of the worlds. Whoever knows Me thus is undeluded among human beings and is freed from all sins.

लोकमहेश्वरतामेव स्फुटयति -- बुद्धिरिति त्रिभिः। बुद्धिः सारासारविवेकनैपुण्यम्? ज्ञानमात्मविषयम्? असंमोहो व्याकुलत्वाभावः? क्षमा सहिष्णुत्वम्? सत्यं यथार्थभाषणम्? दमो बाह्येन्द्रियसंयमः? शमोऽन्तःकरणसंयमः? सुखमनुकूलसंवेदनीयम्? दुःखं च तद्विपरीतम्? भव उद्भवः अभावस्तद्विपरीतः? भयं त्रासः? अभयं तद्विपरीतम्। अस्य लोकस्य मत्त एव भवन्तीत्युत्तरेणान्वयः।

He makes His status as great Lord of the worlds explicit in three verses. ‘Intellect’ is skill in discriminating the essential from the nonessential; ‘knowledge’ concerns the Self; ‘non-delusion’ is absence of bewilderment; ‘forbearance’ is endurance; ‘truth’ is speaking what accords with reality; ‘control’ is restraint of the outer senses; ‘calmness’ is restraint of the inner faculty; ‘pleasure’ is an agreeable experience and ‘pain’ its opposite; ‘becoming’ is arising and ‘non-becoming’ its opposite; ‘fear’ is dread and ‘fearlessness’ its opposite. These states of this world arise from Me alone, as connected with the following verse.

किंच -- अहिंसेति। अहिंसा परपीडानिवृत्तिः? समता रागद्वेषादिराहित्यं? मित्रामित्रतुल्यता च? तुष्टिर्दैवलब्धेन संतोषः? तपः शारीरादि वक्ष्यमाणम्? दानं न्यायार्जितधनादेः सत्पात्रार्पणम्? यशः सत्कीर्तिः? अयशोऽपकीर्तिः? एते बुद्धिर्ज्ञानमित्यादयस्तद्विपरीताश्चाबुद्ध्यादयो नानाविधा भावाः प्राणिनां मत्तः सकाशादेव भवन्ति।

Further: non-injury is refraining from hurting others; equanimity is freedom from attachment and aversion and equality toward friend and enemy; contentment is satisfaction with what comes by destiny; austerity is bodily and the other kinds to be described later; charity is giving lawfully acquired wealth and the like to a worthy recipient; fame is good reputation and infamy bad reputation. These states—intellect, knowledge and the rest, together with their opposites such as lack of intellect—arise in living beings from Me alone.

किंच -- महर्षय इति। सप्त महर्षयोभृग्वादयः सप्त ब्राह्मणा इत्येते पुराणे निश्चयं गता इत्यादि पुराणप्रसिद्धाः। तेभ्योऽपि पूर्वेऽन्ये चत्वारो महर्षयः सनकादयः? तथा मनवः स्वायंभुवादयः मद्भावा मदीयो भावः प्रभावो येषु ते हिरण्यगर्भात्मनो ममैव मनसः संकल्पमात्राज्जाताः। प्रभावमेवाह -- येषामिति। येषां भृग्वादीनां च सनकादीनां चेमा ब्राह्मणाद्या लोके वर्धमाना यथायथं पुत्रपौत्रादिरूपाः शिष्यादिरूपाश्च प्रजा जाता वर्तन्ते।

Further, the seven great seers such as Bhṛgu are the seven Brāhmaṇas established in Purāṇic tradition; before them were the other four great seers, Sanaka and the rest, and the Manus such as Svāyambhuva. They are ‘of My being,’ possessing My power, born merely from the thought of My mind in the form of Hiraṇyagarbha. He states their power: from those such as Bhṛgu and Sanaka the populations of this world—Brāhmaṇas and the others—have arisen and continue to increase respectively as sons, grandsons, disciples and so forth.
यथोक्तविभूत्यादितत्त्वज्ञानस्य फलमाह -- एतामिति। एतां भृग्वादिलक्षणां मम विभूतिं? योगं चैश्वर्यलक्षणं तत्त्वतो यो वेत्ति सोऽविकम्पेन निःसंशयेन योगेन सम्यग्दर्शनेन युक्तो भवति। नास्त्यत्र संशयः।

He states the fruit of true knowledge of the manifestations and divine power just described. Whoever knows in truth this manifestation of Mine characterized by Bhṛgu and the rest, and My yoga characterized by lordship, becomes united with unwavering, doubt-free yoga, namely right vision. There is no doubt about this.

यथा च विभूतियोगयोर्ज्ञानेन सम्यग्ज्ञानावाप्तिस्तद्दर्शयति -- अहमित्यादिचतुर्भिः। अहं सर्वस्य जगतः प्रभवो भृग्वादिरूपविभूतिद्वारेणोत्पत्तिहेतुः। मत्त एव चास्य सर्वस्यबुद्धिर्ज्ञानमसंमोहः इत्यादि सर्वं प्रवर्तत इति? एवं मत्वाऽवबुध्य बुधा विवेकिनो भावसमन्विताः प्रीतियुक्ता मां भजन्ते।

He shows in four verses beginning ‘I am the source’ how knowledge of His manifestations and yoga leads to right knowledge. I am the source of the whole universe, the cause of its arising through manifestations such as Bhṛgu, and from Me alone all of it proceeds—intellect, knowledge, non-delusion and the rest. Knowing and understanding thus, the wise and discriminating, endowed with loving feeling, worship Me.

प्रीतिपूर्वकं भजनमेवाह -- मच्चित्ता इति। मय्येव चित्तं येषां ते मच्चित्ताः। मामेव गताः प्राप्ताः प्राणा इन्द्रियाणि येषां ते मद्गतप्राणाः मदर्पितजीवना इति वा। एवंभूतास्ते बुधाः अन्योन्यं मां न्यायोपेतैः श्रुत्यादिप्रमाणैर्बोधयन्तः? बुद्ध्या च मां कथयन्तः संकीर्तयन्तः सन्तो नित्यं तुष्यन्त्यनुमोदनेन तुष्टिं यान्ति। रमन्ति च निर्वृत्तिं यान्ति।

He explains worship performed with love. Those whose minds are in Me alone are ‘Me-minded’; those whose vital powers and senses have reached Me are ‘whose life-breaths are devoted to Me,’ or whose very lives are offered to Me. Such wise persons enlighten one another about Me through scripture and other valid means supported by reasoning, speak of and glorify Me with understanding, and constantly become satisfied through mutual appreciation; they delight and attain fulfilment.
एवंभूतानां च सम्यग्ज्ञानमहं ददामीत्याह -- तेषामिति। एवं सततयुक्तानां मय्यासक्तानां प्रीतिपूर्वकं भजतां तेषां तं बुद्धिरूपं योगमुपायं ददामि। तमिति कम्। येनोपायेन ते भक्ता मां प्राप्नुवन्ति।

He says that He gives right knowledge to such devotees. To those who are constantly united, attached to Me, and worship with love, I give that yoga in the form of understanding, that means by which those devotees attain Me.

बुद्धियोगं दत्त्वा च तस्यानुभवपर्यन्तं तमापाद्याविद्याकृतं संसारं नाशयामीत्याह -- तेषामिति। तेषामनुकम्पार्थमनुग्रहार्थमेवाज्ञानाज्जातं तमः संसाराख्यं नाशयामि। कुत्र वा स्थितः सन्केन साधनेन तमो नाशयसीत्यत,आह। आत्मभावस्थः बुद्धिवृत्तौ स्थितः सन् भास्वता विस्फुरता ज्ञानलक्षणेन दीपेन नाशयामि।

Having given the yoga of understanding and brought it to the point of direct experience, He says that He destroys saṃsāra produced by ignorance. Solely out of compassion and grace toward them, I destroy the darkness called saṃsāra that has arisen from ignorance. Asked where He is situated and by what means He destroys this darkness, He says: abiding in their inner being, situated in the movement of their intellect, I destroy it with the radiant, shining lamp whose nature is knowledge.
संक्षेपेणोक्ता विभूतीर्विस्तरेण जिज्ञासुर्भगवन्तं स्तुवन्नर्जुन उवाच -- परं ब्रह्मेति सप्तभिः। परं ब्रह्म च? परं धाम च आश्रयः? परमं च पवित्रं भवा�...

Desiring to know in detail the manifestations stated briefly, Arjuna praises the Lord in seven verses beginning ‘Supreme Brahman.’ You are the Supreme Brahman, the supreme abode and support, and the supreme purifier. Why? Because they declare You to be the eternal Person, divine, self-luminous, the primal God—the origin of the gods—unborn and all-pervading.
के त इत्यत आह -- आहुरिति। ऋषयः भृग्वादयः सर्वे देवर्षिर्नारदः असितश्च देवलश्च व्यासश्च स्वयं त्वमेव साक्षान्मे मह्यं ब्रवीषि।
Who says this? All the seers such as Bhṛgu, the divine seer Nārada, Asita, Devala and Vyāsa, and You Yourself directly tell me so.

अतो ममेदानीं त्वदैश्वर्येऽसंभावना निवृत्तेत्याह -- सर्वमिति। एतद्भवानेव परं ब्रह्मेत्यादि सर्वमप्यृतं सत्यं मन्ये यन्मां प्रति त्वं कथयसिन मे विदुः सुरगणा इत्यादि तदपि सत्यमेव मन्य इत्याह -- न हीति। हे भगवन्? तव व्यक्तिं देवा न विदुः। अस्मदनुग्रहार्थमियमभिव्यक्तिरिति न जानन्ति। दानवाश्चास्मन्निग्रहार्थमिति न विदुरेवेति।

He says that now his doubt concerning the Lord’s majesty has ceased. I regard as true everything You tell me—that You are the Supreme Brahman and so forth; and I also regard as true what You say, ‘the hosts of gods do not know Me.’ O Lord, the gods do not understand Your manifestation as being for our grace, nor do the demons understand it as being for our restraint and punishment.

किं तर्हि -- स्वयमिति। स्वयमेव त्वमात्मानं वेत्थ जानासि नान्यः तदप्यात्मना स्वेनैव वेत्थ न साधनान्तरेण। अत्यादरेण बहुधा संबोधयति हे पुरुषोत्तम। पुरुषोत्तमत्वे हेतुगर्भाणि संबोधनानि। हे भूतभावन भूतोत्पादक भूतानामीश नियन्तः? देवानामादित्यादीनां देव प्रकाशक? जगत्पते विश्वपालक।

What then? You alone know Yourself; no other knows You. And You know Yourself by Yourself, not through some other means. Out of great reverence Arjuna addresses Him repeatedly: O Supreme Person. The other vocatives contain reasons for His being the Supreme Person: O producer of beings, O ruler and controller of beings, O God who illumines the gods such as the Ādityas, O Lord and protector of the universe.
यस्मात्तवाभिव्यक्तिं त्वमेव वेत्सि न देवादयस्तस्माद्वक्तुमर्हसीति या आत्मनस्तव दिव्या अत्यद्भुता विभूतयस्ताः सर्वा वक्तुं त्वमेवार्हसि योग्यो भवसि। याभिरिति विभूतीनां विशेषणं स्पष्टार्थम्।

Since You alone know Your manifestation and not the gods and others, You alone are fit and able to declare fully all those divine, exceedingly wondrous manifestations of Yourself. ‘By which’ is simply a qualifier of those manifestations.
कथनप्रयोजनं दर्शयन्प्रार्थयते -- कथमिति द्वाभ्याम्। हे योगिन्? कथं कैर्विभूतिभेदैः सदा परिचिन्तयन्नहं त्वां विद्यां जानीयाम्। विभूतिभेदेन चिन्त्योऽपि त्वं केषु केषु पदार्थेषु मया चिन्तनीयोऽसि।

Showing the purpose of the requested description, Arjuna asks in two verses beginning ‘How?’ O Yogin, by contemplating You constantly, through which particular manifestations may I know You? In which specific objects should I contemplate You as manifested in distinct forms?

तदेवं बहिर्मुखेऽपि चित्ते तत्र तत्र विभूतिभेदेन त्वच्चिन्तैव यथा भवेत्तथा विस्तरेण कथयेत्याह -- विस्तरेणेति। आत्मनस्तव योगं सर्वज्ञत्वसर्वशक्तित्वादिलक्षणं योगैश्वर्यं विभूतिं च विस्तरेण पुनः कथय। हि यस्मात्त्वद्वाक्यममृतरूपं शृण्वतो मम तृप्तिरलंबुद्धिर्नास्ति।

Thus Arjuna asks Him to speak in detail so that even when the mind turns outward, it may still contemplate Him in each object through His distinct manifestations. Tell me again in detail Your yoga, the lordly power characterized by omniscience, omnipotence and the like, and Your manifestations. For while hearing Your words, which are nectar, I have no satiety or feeling that it is enough.

एवं प्रार्थितः सन् श्रीभगवानुवाच -- हन्तेति। हन्तेत्यनुकम्पासंबोधनम्। दिव्या या मम विभूतयस्ताः प्राधान्येन तुभ्यं कथयिष्यामि। यतोऽवान्तरस्य विभूतिविस्तरस्य मदीयस्यान्तो नास्त्यतः प्रधानभूताः कतिचिद्वर्णयिष्यामि।

Thus requested, the Blessed Lord says ‘Very well.’ ‘Hanta’ is an expression of compassionate address. I shall tell you My divine manifestations chiefly and selectively. Since there is no end to the detailed extent of My manifestations, I shall describe only some principal ones.

तत्र प्रथममैश्वरं रूपं कथयति -- अहमिति। हे गुडाकेश? सर्वेषां भूतानामाशयेष्वन्तःकरणेषु सर्वज्ञत्वादिगुणैर्नियन्तृत्वेनावस्थितः परमात्माहम्। आदिर्जन्म? मध्यं स्थितिः? अन्तः संहारः? सर्वभूतानां जन्मादिहेतुश्चाहमेवेत्यर्थः।

First He describes His primary lordly form. O Guḍākeśa, I am the Supreme Self abiding in the hearts and inner faculties of all beings as their ruler, endowed with omniscience and the other divine qualities. ‘Beginning’ is birth, ‘middle’ is continuance, and ‘end’ is dissolution; I alone am the cause of the birth, continuance and dissolution of all beings.
